walkthrough:
Equate the sum to infinity formulas for progressions $P$ and $Q$:
$$S_P = \frac{6}{1 - r}, \quad S_Q = \frac{12}{1 - (-r)} = \frac{12}{1 + r}$$
$$\frac{6}{1 - r} = \frac{12}{1 + r}$$

Cross-multiply and solve for the common ratio $r$:
$$6(1 + r) = 12(1 - r) \implies 1 + r = 2(1 - r) \implies 1 + r = 2 - 2r \implies 3r = 1 \implies r = \frac{1}{3}$$

hints: Substitute $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ to form a quadratic in $\cos\theta$.
Factorise and find both solutions for $\theta \in [0, \pi]$.
walkthrough:
Set up the sum formula $S_{13}$ for the arithmetic progression with $a = \cos\theta$ and $d = \sin^2\theta$:
$$S_{13} = \frac{13}{2}\left(2\cos\theta + 12\sin^2\theta\right) = 13\left(\cos\theta + 6\sin^2\theta\right) = 52$$

Simplify and substitute the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$:
$$\cos\theta + 6\sin^2\theta = 4 \implies \cos\theta + 6(1 - \cos^2\theta) = 4$$
$$6\cos^2\theta - \cos\theta - 2 = 0$$

Solve for the possible values of $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{2}{3} \quad\text{or}\quad \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Find the solutions for $\theta$ in the interval $0 \le \theta \le \pi$ in radians:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{2}{3} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 0.841\text{ rad}$$
$$\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3} \approx 2.09\text{ rad}$$
